task.goal: Ship all 100 packages within 25 minutes with at most 1 mis-sort and nothing damaged.

comparators.label: Code heuristic: pack stations accept all sizes
Random hill-climber at equal budget (23 sim evals)

accepted.rationale: Add a fifth pack station at (14,7) adjacent to the sorter to further balance pack load and shorten pack->ship routes for zone A, while keeping all stations at least 2 cells apart. This should reduce makespan and damage by cutting travel and queueing.

rejected.rationale: Improved training objective (12753 vs 18655) and eliminated mis-sorts. Added L coverage and a third pack station to reduce pack congestion and wait; moved sorter centrally to shorten routes. Damaged packages remain the main gap, so this layout is the best tested candidate to submit.
rejected.reason: not the best proposal this generation (train 12753.67)

rejected.rationale: Add pack-6 at (18,7) to spread pack load and shorten routes to ship-A, while keeping all fixed docks and the sorter at (12,7). This follows VER-g1's evidence that adding pack stations sharply reduces objective, and the FLOW lens of spreading load so no queue explodes.
rejected.reason: not the best proposal this generation (train 12010.83)

rejected.rationale: Adding a sixth pack station at (20,11) near ship-A to reduce pack-side congestion and travel for A-zone packages, and enabling L on the two previously S/M-only pack stations so every package size has coverage. This addresses the CAPACITY/COVERAGE lens: more pack capacity and full size/zone acceptance should lower makespan and keep mis-sorts at zero, though fragile damage remains a separate risk not addressed by this layout.

This improves size coverage and capacity while keeping capex under the $300k cap. Damage remains the main objective driver, so I also keep the verified good pack locations from VER-g1.
